figures_and_tables.caption_draft: Compiled full-wrapper circuit prices for fixed H4. Pauli-JW circuits are shown separately for generic whole-body control and central-rotation control; DF-native circuits use their saved native construction. PF prices are deterministic singleton counts, whereas PR prices are saved means over 256 trajectories. Error bars on PR means denote saved nominal Student-t 95% half-widths, not rigorous bounds on population costs or unseen events. Cosine and sine prices coincide in the saved cohort. State preparation is excluded, and the different splits, event laws and control constructions prevent a representation-only interpretation.

figures_and_tables.caption_draft: Pauli control synthesis on saved bodies and trajectories. The saved panels show central-control PR prices, per-trajectory reductions relative to the same-ID generic circuits, and reference circuit prices. The D2 singleton contrasts give PF prices of 255500 versus 15028 RZ and PR-index0 prices of 9652 versus 1145 RZ for generic versus central control. The contrasts hold the body, trajectory, angles and compiler settings fixed; they measure the combined effect of control construction and compiler response. The DF reference cohort is unpaired. Histogram bins and summaries are reused from the saved analysis; they do not establish population-tail bounds.

figures_and_tables.caption_draft: Conditional total RZ resources at five saved signal tolerances. Left: saved prices combined with the saved shot sufficient condition on the hypothetical zero-implementation-residual slice. Right: the three specified central-control comparisons at each tolerance, with ranges over independent method- and axis-specific residual guard boxes. These ranges are deterministic sensitivity ranges, not statistical confidence intervals. All comparisons keep the saved circuit-price means fixed. Selected later Arb enclosures cover the central PF singleton and PR indices 0 and 1 on both axes; they do not establish PR-law residuals or authorize replacing the hypothetical slice by actual residuals. Population-cost tails and an unconditional end-to-end advantage remain unresolved. Lines connect saved conditions for display only.

Nine configurations were measured, including the four full circuits, retained-only and event-only PR-index0 circuits, and an empty wrapper. The separately displayed saved interaction is Δ=C_full−C_retained−C_event+C_empty. It measures nonadditivity in the full construction and compilation context, rather than a uniquely attributable basis or compiler-pass cost. These ablations are diagnostics, not valid alternative simulation algorithms. The initial Pauli-PR historical fingerprint failure remains unresolved; the successful later criterion-B run does not recover the missing old program. Pauli values in this diagnostic use generic control.
